test_title: PYST 38: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 28 Oct, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: english
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
solution:
The correct answer is '**bigger**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence states: "He might have been referred to as the Pocket Dynamo, but his deeds dwarfed those of far (2) _________ athletes in his sport."
 
• The word "dwarfed" means to make something seem small by comparison. This implies a comparison between Jadhav's achievements and those of other athletes.
 
• The phrase "far _________ athletes" suggests a comparison in size or physical stature, especially considering his nickname "Pocket Dynamo." It implies that even athletes who were physically larger (bigger) than him did not achieve as much.
 
• "**Bigger**" (बड़ा) is the comparative form of "big," and it correctly sets up the comparison that his deeds surpassed those of athletes who were physically larger.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

Complete Passage: *Khashaba Jadhav was the independent India's first individual olympic medallist. There (1) **are **__some firsts that stay in history forever. The one held by Khashaba Jadhav is one such first. He might have been referred to as the Pocket Dynamo, but his deeds dwarfed those of far (2)__bigger__ athletes in his sport. Just a couple of years after India had become a Republic, Jadhav took part in the 1952 Olympics at Helsinki, Finland. As funding sportspersons weren't really a (3) _________ for a country just finding its feet, Jadhav’s trip to Helsinki was actually funded by the public. Jadhav however, (4) _________ his way to fame, becoming independent India's first individual Olympic medal winner. He (5) _________ bronze in the bantamweight category.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "smaller"** – If he was "Pocket Dynamo" and his deeds dwarfed smaller athletes, it wouldn't make sense; his deeds dwarfed those who were ostensibly more physically imposing.
 
• **Option 2: "big"** – This is the positive degree. The phrase "far big athletes" is grammatically incorrect and doesn't establish the necessary comparison.
 
• **Option 3: "small"** – This is the positive degree. "Far small athletes" is grammatically awkward and doesn't fit the comparison.

44:T
